subject: PolarisBank: request to prioritize tenant-affinity & routing SLA for activation
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@polarisbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: PolarisBank: request to prioritize tenant-affinity & routing SLA for activation

Team —

Quick context: PolarisBank (HS-9876543) is moving from pilot to production with a targeted go-live in Q1. Procurement has asked for deterministic request routing (tenant affinity / pinning) and a per-tenant routing SLA so they can satisfy regulatory audit requirements. They are committing to a 12-month contract with an ARR expectation of ~$1.1M if we can meet the activation timeline + routing guarantees.

Attachments: Polaris_MAP_v2.pdf (mutual action plan + timeline), Polaris_SOW_redlined.pdf (redlines from procurement).

Asking Product/Engineering: can we table this as a prioritized sprint activity for the Dec planning window? Specifically we need: 
- Tenant-affinity routing (session pinning to a warm pool) with a documented fallback policy.
- Route-level SLA (P99 < 200ms for inference under typical QPS) and trace propagation for audit logs.

Business impact: Polaris will gate their cross-bank rollouts on these capabilities. We expect expansion to other business units if we hit their go-live.

What I need from you by EOD Tues: a short note on feasibility + rough dev effort (S, M, L) and whether an MVP staged approach is acceptable (minimal safety-first rollout vs full deterministic guarantee). I can reframe the MAP if you want different acceptance criteria.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PolarisBank: request to prioritize tenant-affinity & routing SLA for activation

Thanks for the heads-up, Monica — and congrats on the large ARR upside. A few clarifying questions so we can scope a sensible MVP: 

1) Traffic profile: what is the expected sustained QPS and burst patterns for the initial rollout? Any 95/99 token-per-request distributions?
2) Data residency / compliance constraints: are they requesting private VPC or is hosted with stricter audit hooks sufficient?
3) Failure modes: procurement mentions "deterministic routing" — do they need hard guarantees (no failover) or an auditable deterministic attempt + documented fallback sequence?

From a product perspective I want to separate: 
- MVP (soft-affinity + detailed audit logs + fallback policy documented) — lower engineering risk and might be acceptable to procurement as a contractual "designated approach" with a phased SLA ramp.
- Full deterministic pinning (stateful, strong guarantees across autoscale) — higher infra complexity and will take more cycles.

Next steps: Marcus, can you give a quick engineering feasibility note and a ballpark effort estimate for both MVP and full deterministic option? Also file a Jira (INF-XXXX) so we can track scope, QA, and rollout checklist. Monica — please push Polaris to confirm whether a phased SLA is contractually acceptable (we can accept a ramp to full P99 SLA).

Irene
Irene Choi | Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PolarisBank: request to prioritize tenant-affinity & routing SLA for activation

Quick technical readout: high level this is feasible but non-trivial. Notes below: 

- MVP approach (recommended as decoupled path):
  * Implement session affinity using a warm-pool tagging + best-effort KV cache for affinity.
  * Emit per-request trace-id and routing decision logs to audit sink (s3/kafka) with retention policy.
  * Fallback: if warm pool unavailable, route to nearest compatible variant and flag metric + alert.
  * Rough eng estimate: 3-4 sprints (6-8 engineering-weeks) across serving + runtime + infra work.

- Full deterministic pinning:
  * Requires stateful routing layer and cross-node affinity coordination (consistent hashing + lease).
  * Needs expanded testing for autoscale, failure injection, and significant QA windows.
  * Rough eng estimate: 8-12 sprints (roughly 16-24 engineering-weeks) and ops readiness.

Open questions / risks:
- Willingness to accept a ramped SLA in contract (MVP -> full deterministic) to reduce time-to-activation.
- Observability & trace retention cost; procurement asked for a 13-month retention which will increase storage costs — need finance signoff if we bake into the deal.

I can draft an INF ticket (INF-4321) this morning with acceptance criteria and a proposed 3-phase rollout (MVP canary in one region -> regional rollouts -> deterministic guarantee). Laura, from a CS perspective can you confirm whether Polaris will accept a canary in one business unit? Monica, if you can get contractual confirmation on the ramp approach we can lock down estimates for the SOW.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@polarisbank.com>, PolarisBank Procurement <procurement@polarisbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PolarisBank: request to prioritize tenant-affinity & routing SLA for activation

Thanks all — quick update after yesterday's procurement call with Polaris: they will accept a phased SLA if the MAP clearly calls out the ramp schedule and canary acceptance criteria. Procurement asked specifically for
- a canary in a non-customer-facing BU for 4 weeks,
- P99 target of < 250ms during canary (they're willing to accept a 30% ramp tolerance in month 1),
- 13-month trace retention for audit evidence (we'll need to bill retention as an add-on if ops cost is significant).

I've attached the updated MAP and the redlined SOW they returned this morning (Polaris_MAP_v2.pdf, Polaris_SOW_redlined.pdf). HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543.

Action items agreed: 
- Marcus: create INF-4321 with the MVP acceptance criteria and estimated timeline (target: draft by 11/22).
- Irene: prioritize INF-4321 into Dec planning and confirm whether Product can earmark a single sprint for initial infra work.
- Laura: prepare CS canary runbook and rollback plan (include audit evidence checklist).
- Monica: I will coordinate contract language for the ramped SLA and secure procurement sign-off on charging for trace retention.

If Product/Eng confirm MVP sizing is S/M/L asap we can propose the activation date internally during next week's roadmap sync.

Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Polaris contact: Ethan Lowe | ethan.lowe@polarisbank.com
